questions.prompt: What does he say is most important at the pattern level for health/longevity diets?
choices: A Maximizing ultra-processed foods.
B Dietary pattern overall—healthy patterns are generally very low in ultra-processed foods.
C Only counting grams of salt.
D Eating identical macros for every person.
questions.explain: Dietary pattern is central; healthy longevity patterns are low in UPFs.

questions.prompt: On 'a calorie is a calorie,' his nuance is:
choices: A Calories do not exist.
B Energy units are equal, but 100 kcal of fries is not the same biologically as 100 kcal of eggs.
C Only fries provide usable energy.
D Eggs have zero calories.
questions.explain: Calorie units match, but food matrix and effects differ.

questions.prompt: Which trio does he call the major satiety superstars?
choices: A Sugar, alcohol, and salt.
B Protein, fiber, and water.
C Only fat and caffeine.
D Artificial colors and emulsifiers.
questions.explain: Protein, fiber, and water; protein is the most satiating macronutrient.

questions.prompt: Fat-soluble vitamins he flags to ingest with fat are:
choices: A B vitamins only.
B A, E, D, and K.
C Vitamin C and folate only.
D None—fat blocks absorption.
questions.explain: A, E, D, and K should be taken with food/fat.

B It is a cofactor in hundreds (about 300+) of processes; many adults underconsume it.
C Only athletes need it once yearly.
D It replaces all protein needs.
